Shows today's activity (Arrivals today and pending check-ins, Departures today and pending check-outs, Guests in house and Average rate), the occupancy charts by status and by room type, arrivals and departures for the next 7 days, the most occupied rooms of the last 90 days, the expected occupancy for the next 14 days, the monthly occupancy of the last 12 months (including confirmed bookings for the current month) and the average length of stay.

It has its own period. Shows New guests, Returning guests, Return rate and Average spend, plus the booking profile: Average stay, Average lead time (days between booking and arrival), Guests per booking and % of bookings with children.

The charts show the top spending guests (lodging plus services; hover to see the breakdown), guests by age (holders and companions), guests by nationality and group composition (solo traveler, couple, with children or group of adults).

With its own period, it shows Services income (room service and upgrades), Room service orders (undelivered and average ticket), Upgrades (and relocations without charge), Stays with consumption and Average delivery, plus the charts of services income, most ordered products, orders by time of day, upgrades by room type and room service delivery time.

At the bottom, "Pending orders now" lists the orders waiting for delivery (green, orange or red depending on how long ago they were placed) and "Latest room changes" the upgrades and relocations of the period. The "View orders" and "View log" buttons open those screens (if you have permission). The "Services report" button opens that report in Reports with the same period.

pasos: Open the Dashboard from the "Dashboard" button in the side menu.
On the General tab, check the current room status on the top cards.
Choose a period with the shortcuts or with From/To and press "Refresh".
Review the revenue, the spending source and the payments of the period.
Switch to Occupancy, Guests or Services to see the other indicators.
If you need the printed detail, press "Generate report" (or "Services report" on the Services tab).

elementos.texto: Switch between General, Occupancy, Guests and Services. The active tab is shown in gold and its data is reloaded when opened.
Current number of available, occupied, for cleaning and under maintenance rooms (out of the total), and the occupancy rate of the active capacity.
Fill From/To with today, the last 7 or 30 days or the current month and recalculate the revenue immediately.
Calculates the indicators over the hotel's whole history; the dates are disabled and the button turns gold.
Custom period. Pressing "Refresh" recalculates the indicators; the From date cannot be later than To.
Contains the period filters and the "Generate report" button, which opens Reports on the Bookings report with the chosen period and generates it directly.
Period revenue (payments), Average ticket, % cancelled reservations and Cancelled amount for the selected period.
Donut chart that splits what was collected between Booking, Renewal, Room Service and Room upgrades, with the total in the center and a legend with amounts.
Today's movement, occupancy by status and by type, expected occupancy for the next 14 days (hover over a bar to see how many rooms) and average length of stay.
Its own period with shortcuts, cards for new and returning guests, return rate, average spend per guest and the nationality chart.
Room service and upgrade indicators and charts for the chosen period, with the "Services report" button.

consejos: You need the permission to view the Dashboard. "Generate report" requires the permission to generate the bookings report and "Services report" the permission to generate the services report.
The status cards reflect the current moment and do not depend on the chosen period.
To compare months, use "This month" and then a From/To range for the previous month.

temas.resumen: Screen to generate the hotel's printable reports: choose the report on a tab, set the filters and see the preview ready to print or save as PDF.

parrafos: At the top are the Bookings, Services by guest and Predictive analysis tabs (only those you are allowed to use). On the left is the tab's panel with its title, a description, the filters and the "Generate report" button; a summary of the result appears below the button (for example the number of bookings and nights sold).
On the right is the preview with its pages. Each tab remembers the last report you generated, so you can switch between them without losing it.

Bookings: From, To, shortcuts (This month, Last 30 days, This year), "Full history" and Booking status. Services by guest: the same periods plus Service type, Service status and Guest (ID, first or last name).
Predictive analysis: Forecast period (next 14, 30, 60 or 90 days), History to analyze (last 6, 12 or 24 months or the full history) and Room type (or all room types).

The preview bar lets you change pages, zoom in or out (also with Ctrl + mouse wheel), "Fit width", "Save PDF" (uses the "Microsoft Print to PDF" printer and lets you choose where to save it) and "Print" (opens the dialog to choose a printer).
If there is no data for the selected filters, the panel says so and the preview stays empty. When you change the language, reports already generated are rebuilt in the new language.

pasos: Open Reports from the "Reports" button in the side menu (or from "Generate report" on the Dashboard).
Choose the tab of the report you need.
Fill in the filters: period or "Full history", status and other options.
Press "Generate report" and read the summary shown below the button.
Review the preview: change pages, zoom or "Fit width".
Press "Save PDF" to get the file or "Print" to send it to a printer.

elementos.texto: Choose the report: Bookings, Services by guest or Predictive analysis. Only the ones you are allowed to use are shown; the active one is marked with a gold line.

Period of the bookings report (by check-in date) or the services report (by service date). The start date cannot be later than the end date. Below are the This month, Last 30 days and This year shortcuts.
Ignores the dates and uses the hotel's whole history; the dates are disabled while it is checked.
Limits the bookings report to one status: Pending, Occupied, Finished or Cancelled. "All" includes every booking.
Filter the services report by type (Room service or Room upgrade) and by status (Requested, Delivered or Completed).
Searches for a guest by ID, first or last name (up to 100 characters). Enter generates the report.
Forecast period (14, 30, 60 or 90 days from today), History to analyze (6, 12 or 24 months or the full history) and Room type to analyze.
Builds the report with the tab's filters, shows it in the preview and writes a summary below. It validates the period and the report permission.
Shows the pages of the generated report exactly as they will be printed. If you have not generated one yet, it tells you what to do.
Move through the report pages; "Page X of Y" is shown next to them.
The + and − buttons zoom in or out (also Ctrl + mouse wheel). "Fit width" fits the page to the width of the viewer.

Saves the report as PDF with the "Microsoft Print to PDF" printer: choose the folder and name, and you can open it when it finishes. If that printer is not installed, use "Print" and choose another PDF printer.
Opens the print dialog to choose the printer and send the report.

consejos: Each tab requires its permission: generate the bookings report, generate the services report or generate the demand analysis.
Files are suggested with a name and date (for example Reporte_reservas_YYYYMMDD_HHMM), so they do not overwrite each other.
From the Dashboard, "Generate report" and "Services report" open this screen with the same period already loaded.

temas.resumen: Printed report with the bookings whose check-in date falls within the chosen period, with nights, billing, payments and outstanding balance.

parrafos: The first page has the "HORIZON HOTEL & RESORT — Reservations report" band, the period (or "all-time") and the criterion: reservations with check-in date within the period.

Then six summary cards: RESERVATIONS (broken down into pending, occupied, finished and cancelled), ROOM NIGHTS SOLD (and the average per booking), BILLED (excluding cancellations), COLLECTED (recorded payments), OUTSTANDING BALANCE (due at check-out) and CANCELLATION RATE.

One row per reservation, sorted by check-in date, with the #, Guest, Document, Room, Type, Check-in, Check-out, Nights, Guests, Status, Total, Paid and Balance columns. The status is colored, outstanding balances are highlighted in red and cancelled reservations are grey.
At the end the Totals row adds up Total, Paid and Balance. If the table spans several sheets, the header is repeated and each page shows at the bottom who generated it, the date and "Page X of Y".
Nights sold, billing and balance exclude cancelled reservations; the collected amount includes every recorded payment (for example, a deposit on a reservation later cancelled).

pasos: In Reports, choose the Bookings tab.
Choose From and To, a shortcut, or check "Full history".
Optionally filter by Booking status.
Press "Generate report" and review the preview.
Save it as PDF or print it.
consejos: You need the permission to generate the bookings report.
To check balances to be collected, filter by the Occupied status: those are the stays in progress that pay the balance at check-out.

temas.resumen: Printed report with the room service and upgrades charged to each stay, grouped by guest with their running total and the status of each service.

parrafos: The top band shows the period and the criteria used (Type, Status and Guest). Below are six cards: Services total (services and stays), Room service (orders and how many are not delivered yet), Upgrades (category changes), Guests with charges (and average per guest), Share of billing (services as a percentage of lodging plus services) and Average delivery (minutes from order to room).
If the report includes room service, a line with the most ordered items is added.

Each guest has a title with their name, ID, guest number and number of services and stays. Below are their services with Date, Room, Service type, Description (for example "Room service order #00012" or "Upgrade to Suite"), Quantity / details (items in the order, or previous → new room, nights and rate difference), Status and Amount.

Each group ends with the guest's accumulated total and the report ends with the grand total. A guest's title is never left alone at the bottom of a sheet: if the services continue on the next one, the title is repeated with "(continued)".
Requested: room service order entered and not delivered yet. Delivered: order already taken to the room. Completed: a service fulfilled when it is registered, such as an upgrade.

pasos: In Reports, choose the Services by guest tab.
Choose the period or check "Full history".
Optionally filter by Service type, Service status or a Guest.
Press "Generate report" (or Enter in the Guest field).
Review the preview and save it as PDF or print it.
consejos: You need the permission to generate the services report.
Filter by the Requested status to spot room service orders that have not been delivered yet.
Relocations decided by the hotel do not generate a charge, so they do not appear as a service.

temas.resumen: Smart report that forecasts occupancy for the coming days from the history of bookings, stays and spending, detects low occupancy or saturation and suggests prices, promotions and personalized offers.

parrafos: For each future night and each room type, the starting point is the historical occupancy of the same month, adjusted by weekday (Fridays and Saturdays usually fill up more) and by holidays. Rooms already booked are reduced by the historical cancellation rate (stays in progress count in full), and the bookings that usually have not been made yet at that lead time are added (lead-time curve from the history).

So a distant date depends almost only on the history, and a close one mostly on what is already booked. The season (high, mid or low) comes from comparing each month with the average; without history for the month the typical calendar is used (January, February and July are high season). With fewer than 60 nights of history the summary warns that the forecast is indicative.

Thresholds: low occupancy below 40%, high from 75% and saturation from 90%. Price suggestion per night: from 90% raise the rate +20% (with a 2-night minimum stay on Fridays, Saturdays, holidays and holiday eves); between 75% and 90% raise +10% (+15% on those peak days); between 40% and 75% keep it; between 25% and 40% stay + room service bundle (−10%); below 25% a 20% discount with a services package.

Alerts: stretches of 3 or more consecutive low-occupancy days (offer discounts and bundle promotions), saturation days or stretches (raise rates and require a minimum stay) and the Argentine national holidays in the period (New Year, Carnival, Remembrance Day, Malvinas, Holy Week, Labour Day, May Revolution, Güemes, Belgrano, Independence, San Martín, Cultural Diversity, Sovereignty, Immaculate Conception and Christmas).

Summary (Forecast vs. historical occupancy, Low-occupancy days, Saturation days, Most demanded type, Season with the historical cancellation rate and Forecast revenue); Occupancy forecast (bar chart: already booked + expected pickup, with the 40% and 90% lines, Fridays and Saturdays shaded and a gold triangle on holidays); Alerts & recommendations; Day-by-day forecast (season, booked, estimated %, most demanded type, last year, expected spend and suggestion; (H) holiday and (E) holiday eve).

Demand by room type (history, forecast occupancy, current rate and suggested rate); Seasonality (occupancy by month and by weekday); Booking behavior (average and median lead time, length of stay, guests, weekend arrivals); Revenue & spending (accommodation, room service, upgrades, ADR and RevPAR, spending trend and most ordered items); Personalized offers and the "How it is calculated" note.

They are proposed for up to 10 returning guests (2 or more stays), based on their preferred type and month and their spending: if they spend on services at least 30% more than average, a stay + room service package with 15% off spending; if their preferred month is high season, a presale with a locked rate when booking 60 days ahead; if it is low season, a 10% loyalty discount; otherwise, a complimentary upgrade to the next type up.

pasos: In Reports, choose the Predictive analysis tab.
Choose the Forecast period (for example, next 30 days).
Choose the History to analyze (more history gives steadier forecasts).
To analyze a single category, choose the Room type.
Press "Generate report" and read the summary: forecast occupancy, low-occupancy days, saturation days and alerts.
Review the alerts and the day-by-day table to decide rates and promotions; save it as PDF or print it.
consejos: You need the permission to generate the demand analysis.
Suggestions are indicative: apply rate changes in Room types after evaluating them.
Generate the analysis regularly: as bookings come in, the forecast for the nearest days becomes more accurate.

temas.resumen: Shows the full history of each reservation: every time it is created or any of its data changes, the system saves a snapshot of the reservation with the operation, date, time and user. From here you can see a reservation's history and, with the rollback permission, make a previous record active again.

parrafos: Every new reservation and every change to it is recorded automatically (by the database): changes to dates or guests, cancellation, no-show, check-in, check-out, stay extension, upgrade and hotel relocation. A change made directly in the database is recorded too, with the user "Outside the system".

Each record is a full snapshot of the reservation (guest, room, dates, check-in/check-out, status, adults, children, rate and amounts). The active record (✔ in the Act column) is the current state; previous ones are shown in grey as history. No record is ever deleted or edited.
When the log started, every existing reservation received an "Initial load" record with its state at that moment.

The "Operation" column tells what was done in each record (new, modification, cancellation, check-in, check-out, extension, room change...). To see exactly which data changed, select the record: the panel on the right shows before and after, with the modified fields highlighted.
When you select a record, the "Record detail" panel shows each field's value before and after; the fields that changed are highlighted.

secciones.titulo: Rollback: restore a previous record as active
parrafos: If a change was made by mistake, the Administrator or a Supervisor can select a previous record (without ✔ in Act) and press "Restore as active". The reservation gets exactly the data of that record back.

The rollback does not delete or edit the history: the log adds a new record with the operation "Rollback", which becomes the active one, and the one that was active stays as history. The record detail shows which record was restored.

It cannot be restored if the room of that record is taken by another reservation on those dates or is out of service, or if the record is the same as the current state. Additional charges and payments are not changed; if the reservation was in progress, the room states are adjusted automatically (the room left is set to cleaning and the restored one to occupied).

pasos: Open "Reservation change log" from the ANALYSIS section of the side menu.
Type the reservation code or a guest name or room number, and optionally choose an operation and a date range.
Press "Apply" (or Enter in the text fields) to see the records.
Check "Active only" to see just the current state of each reservation.
Select a record to see in the right panel which data changed; "Clear" removes all filters.
To see the full history of a reservation, select one of its records and press "View history".
To recover a previous record (rollback), select it, press "Restore as active" and confirm. The reservation history is shown again with the new record selected.

elementos.texto: Reservation number (digits only). It must be greater than zero.
Searches by the guest's first or last name or by room number or type.
Shows only the records of one operation (for example, Cancellation or Check-in). "All" does not filter.
Limit the records by the date of the change. The start date cannot be later than the end date.
When checked, shows only the current record of each reservation (its current state). It is applied immediately.
Queries the log again with the selected filters.
Clears all filters and shows every record.

One row for every new reservation or change, newest first. The operation is colored (green new reservation and check-in, red cancellation and no-show, gold upgrade and extension, blue check-out and room changes, orange modification). Rollback is shown in purple.
Field by field, the value in the reservation's previous record (Before) and in the selected one (After). Changed fields are highlighted.
Shows the number of records or, with one selected, whether it is the current state of the reservation or a previous one.
Shows every record of the selected reservation (its change history), removing the other filters.

Rollback: makes the selected previous record the current state of the reservation again. It asks for confirmation and adds a new "Rollback" record to the log. Only the Administrator and Supervisors see it (rollback permission).
Closes the log.

consejos: You need the permission to view the reservation change log.

Records are never deleted or edited: changes are made from Reservations, Check-In, Check-Out, Room change or Extend stay, and are recorded automatically. A rollback does not overwrite the history either: it adds a new record.
A record with user "Outside the system" means someone modified the reservation directly in the database: review it with the administrator.

temas.resumen: Groups the system tools: users, audit log, permission roles and families, database backups and inconsistency resolution.

parrafos: The "Administrative" button in the side menu (SYSTEM group) opens the menu with User Management, Audit Log, Access Management (Roles and Families) and Backup Management. The Database inconsistency screen is not in the menu: it appears when logging in if direct modifications to the database are detected.
These screens are meant for the administrator; each option is only shown if you have the matching permission.

temas.resumen: Lets you view, create and modify system users, assign them a role, activate or deactivate them and unlock accounts locked by failed attempts.

parrafos: On the left, the users grid with the All, Active and Blocked filters and the "Number of Users" counter. On the right, the data of the selected user: ID Number, Names, Surnames, Email, Role, Username, Blocked and Active, and the action buttons.
The screen works in three modes shown in the message box: View Mode (selecting a row shows its data), Insert Mode (after pressing "Create") and Edit Mode (after pressing "Modify").

When creating a user you enter ID Number, Names, Surnames, Email and Role. The system generates the Username by joining the ID number and the first name, and an initial password made of the ID number and the surname; the user must change it on first login.

When editing, only the Email and Role can be changed. "Activate/Deactivate" toggles whether the user can log in. "Unlock" enables an account locked after 3 failed attempts within 2 hours and resets it to the initial password. You cannot modify your own role, email or status.

pasos: Open User Management from the "Administrative" button.
To create: press "Create", fill in ID Number (digits only), Names, Surnames, Email and Role, and press "Apply".
To edit: select the user, press "Modify", change Email or Role and press "Apply".
"Cancel" discards the operation and returns to View Mode.
To enable or disable a user, select it and press "Activate" or "Deactivate".
If a user is locked, filter "Blocked", select it, press "Unlock" and tell them to log in with the initial password.

elementos.texto: Lists the users with their data, role and statuses. Selecting a row loads its data on the right and enables the relevant buttons.
Show every user, only active users or only blocked users.
Number of users shown in the grid with the current filter.
The user's personal data, required when creating it. The ID number accepts digits only and cannot be repeated. They cannot be changed later.
The user's email; required and with a valid format. It is one of the two fields that can be modified.
Role that defines the user's permissions. Required; it can be changed in edit mode.
Read-only data: the username generated by the system and the account's current statuses.
"Create" clears the fields and switches to Insert Mode; "Modify" switches to Edit Mode with the selected user. Each requires its permission.
"Apply" validates the data (all fields filled in, valid email and ID number) and saves the new user or the changes. "Cancel" returns to View Mode without saving.
Enabled only if the selected user is blocked. It asks for confirmation, unlocks the user and resets the initial password (ID number + surname).
Toggles the selected user's active status after confirmation. Red means Deactivate and green means Activate.
The box shows whether you are in View, Insert or Edit Mode. "Exit" closes the screen.

consejos: You need the permission to view users; creating, modifying, activating/deactivating and unlocking users are separate permissions.
Every creation, role or email change, lock and unlock is recorded in the Audit Log.
A deactivated user cannot log in even if they know their password; use this option instead of deleting users.

temas.resumen: The "Event Audit" screen shows everything recorded in the system (logins, user changes, permissions, reservations, payments and more) and lets you filter and print it.

parrafos: Each event has the Username of who performed it, the Target Username (the affected user, if any), the DateTime, the Module (Users, Login, Profiles, Reservations, Rooms, Guests, Payments, Configuration or Additional charges), the Event and the Criticality.
Criticality is colored: Critical in red, High in orange, Medium in yellow and Low in green. All events are loaded when the screen opens.

The Module, Event and Criticality lists are linked: choosing a module narrows the event list to that module (and to the chosen criticality); choosing an event fills in its module and criticality automatically.
The date range needs both dates, neither can be later than today and From cannot be later than To.

pasos: Open the Audit Log from the "Administrative" button.
Type the username (or part of it) of who performed the action and/or of the affected user.
Choose the From and To date range.
Choose Module, Event or Criticality depending on what you are looking for.
Press "Filter" to see the results.
Press "Export" to print the grid (or save it as PDF by choosing that printer); "Clear" shows everything again.

elementos.texto: User who performed the action. You can type just part of the name.
User the action was performed on (for example, the user unlocked or modified). Accepts part of the name.
From and To must be filled in together, cannot be later than today and From cannot be later than To.
System area of the event. Choosing it narrows the event list.
Event type (for example failed login or user locked). Choosing it fills in its module and criticality.
Severity of the event: Critical, High, Medium or Low. It also filters the event list.
Validates the dates and shows the events that meet all the filters.
Removes all filters and reloads the full log.
Prints the grid's events on a landscape page; you can choose a PDF printer to save it. It warns you if the grid is empty.
Shows the events with user, affected user, date and time, module, event and colored criticality.

consejos: You need the permission to view the audit log.
To investigate an account lock, filter by Target Username or Username and the Login module.
The log is read-only: no user can modify or delete events from the system.

temas.resumen: Manages the system permissions: families group permissions (and other families) and roles combine families and permissions to be assigned to users.

parrafos: It opens from "Administrative" › "Access Management" › Roles or Families; the title shows "Management of Roles" or "Management of Families". On the left is the List and on the right the Detail: a tree with everything the selected item contains (📁 families and 🔑 permissions).
At the bottom are the Create, Modify and Delete buttons. A role or family in use cannot be deleted (for example, a role assigned to users or a family included in a role).

It has the Name, the Assigned list (what the role or family contains), the Available list and the Selected Item Details, which shows a family's tree or a permission's description. The Add and Delete buttons move components from one list to the other.

The system prevents repeated permissions: Available only lists items that add new permissions; if you add a family that already contains permissions assigned individually, it offers to replace them; and if it conflicts with permissions in another family, it cannot be added. When saving, the name cannot be repeated, there must be at least one permission or family and no other configuration may have exactly the same permissions.

pasos: Open "Administrative" › "Access Management" and choose Roles or Families.
Select an item in the List to see its content in the Detail.
Press "Create" (or select one and press "Modify").
Enter the Name.
Choose components in Available and press "Add"; to remove them, select them in Assigned and press "Delete".
Check the Selected Item Details to confirm which permissions each component includes.
Press "Save"; to discard, press "Cancel".

elementos.texto: Existing roles or families with their name and type. Selecting one shows its content in the Detail.
Shows as a tree the families (📁) and permissions (🔑) contained in the selected role or family.
Open the create window or the modify window for the selected item. They require the permission to create or modify roles or families, depending on the screen.
On the management screen, deletes the selected role or family after confirmation (not possible if it is in use). In the create and modify window, removes the selected component from Assigned.
Name of the role or family. Required and unique among roles and families.
Permissions and families that are part of the role or family you are editing.
Permissions and families that can still be added. Only those that add a permission not yet covered are listed.
Moves the component selected in Available to Assigned. It may suggest a replacement or reject it if it would create repeated permissions.
For a permission it shows its description; for a family, the tree of what it contains.
"Save" validates and stores the role or family; "Cancel" closes without saving.

consejos: You need the permission to view roles or view families; creating, modifying and deleting are separate permissions for each.
If you change the permissions of your own role, your session is invalidated and you must log in again.
Build families by work area (for example, Front desk or Room service) and combine them into roles: it is easier to maintain than assigning individual permissions.

temas.resumen: Creates backups of the hotel database and lets you restore a previous one, with a list of the backups saved in the chosen folder.

parrafos: The card on the left shows the Destination folder (C:\HorizonHotel\Backups by default) and its status: the system validates it when you choose it (it exists or can be created, the path is not too long, there is enough space and the database server can write there). A network folder is accepted with a warning.
It also shows the name the file will have, with the date and time (for example TP_Ing_Soft_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.bak). When it finishes, the result is shown and the new backup appears selected in the list.

The card on the right lets you choose a .bak file (with "Browse" or by double-clicking the list) and shows its name, size and date. Restoring replaces the whole current database with the backup contents: later changes are lost, it cannot be undone and the system restarts when it finishes.
Below, "Saved backups" lists the files in the folder with Date, File, Size and Age, and a summary with the count and total space.

pasos: Open Backup Management from the "Administrative" button.
Check the Destination folder or press "Change" to choose another one and wait for the validation.
Press "Create backup" and read the result.
To restore, double-click a backup in the list or press "Browse" and choose the .bak file.
Check the name, size and date of the chosen file.
Press "Restore this backup" and confirm; the system restarts when it finishes.

elementos.texto: Folder where the backup is saved. "Change" opens the folder picker; it requires the permission to create backups.
Validation result: green if valid, yellow for a warning (for example a network folder) and red if it cannot be used.
Preview of the backup's name, made of the database name and the date and time.
Creates the backup in the chosen folder. It is enabled only with a valid folder and the permission to create backups.
Green or red message with the result of the last backup or restore attempt.
.bak file chosen to restore. "Browse" opens the file picker; it requires the permission to restore.
Name, size and modification date of the chosen backup, to confirm it is the right one.
Reminds you that restoring replaces the whole database, cannot be undone and restarts the system.
Asks for confirmation (with "No" as default) and restores the database from the chosen file; then the application restarts.
Lists the .bak files in the folder with date, file, size and age. Double-click or Enter on one chooses it as the file to restore.
"Open folder" shows the folder in Windows Explorer; "Refresh" reads the backup list again.

consejos: You need the permission to view backups; creating a backup and restoring are separate permissions.
Make a backup before important changes (for example, before restoring another one) and keep a copy outside the computer.
Warn the other users before restoring: the whole database goes back to the backup's state and the application restarts.

temas.resumen: Window shown when logging in if direct modifications to the database (made outside the application) are detected, which lets you resolve them.

parrafos: When you log in, the system checks the verification digits that protect the data. If they do not match, someone modified the database outside the system and login is not allowed.
If your role has the permission to handle inconsistencies, this window opens; otherwise only a notice to contact an administrator is shown.
Recalculate accepts the current data as correct and recalculates the verification digits, without reverting the changes; you can then log in again.

Restore replaces the whole database with a .bak backup you choose (its name, size and date are shown before confirming) and restarts the system. Exit closes the application without resolving anything.

pasos: Read the message and, if possible, find out what change was made to the database.
If the current data is correct, press "Recalculate" and confirm.
If the data was tampered with, press "Restore" and choose the latest trusted backup.
Check the file's name, size and date and confirm; the system restarts.
Log in again.

elementos.texto: Says that direct modifications to the database were detected and that you must choose an action.
Accepts the current data and normalizes the verification digits after confirmation. When it finishes the window closes and you can log in again.
Lets you choose a .bak backup file, shows its details, asks for confirmation and restores the whole database; then it restarts the system.
Closes the application without resolving the inconsistency.

consejos: You need the permission to handle inconsistencies; without it you will only see a notice to contact an administrator.
Recalculate accepts changes that might be improper: use it only if you know what was changed and why.
Keep regular backups: they are the only way to undo an unauthorized modification.

temas.resumen: Groups the options for your own account: change your password, log in again (Relogin) and log out.

parrafos: Open it with the "My profile" button in the side menu or by clicking the card with your initials, name and role. The menu has Change Password, Relogin and Logout. The "Log out" button at the bottom of the side menu also logs out directly.
These options are available to every user, with no special permissions.

temas.resumen: Lets you replace your password with a new one. It is mandatory on first login or after an administrator unlocks your account.

parrafos: You can open it at any time from "My profile" › "Change Password". The system also opens it automatically when you log in if you still have the initial password (ID number + surname), which is assigned when the user is created and when it is unlocked.
After changing it, the session is closed and you must log in again with the new password.

All three fields are required, the new password and the confirmation must match, the new one cannot be the same as the current one and the current password must be correct. The change is recorded in the Audit Log.

pasos: Open "My profile" and choose "Change Password".
Type your Current Password.
Type the New Password and repeat it in Confirm Password (the eye icon shows or hides them).
Press "Change Password".
When "Password Changed" appears, log in again with the new password.

elementos.texto: Your current password. If it is wrong, the change is rejected.
The password you will use from now on; it cannot be the same as the current one. The eye icon shows or hides this field and the confirmation at the same time.
Repeat the new password; it must match exactly.
Validates the three fields and saves the new password. If it succeeds, it closes the window and the session so you log in again.

consejos: No special permission is needed: every user can change their own password.
Use a password that cannot be guessed from your data (avoid your ID number, first name or surname).
If you forgot your password, ask an administrator to unlock your account: you will go back to the initial password and must change it.

temas.resumen: Explains how to log out safely and what the Relogin option in the My profile menu does.

parrafos: You can log out with the "Log out" button at the bottom of the side menu or with "My profile" › "Logout". The system asks for confirmation, records the logout in the Audit Log, saves the language you were using for your next login and returns to the login screen.
Closing the main window with the X also logs you out. The session is closed automatically after changing your password and when you modify the permissions of your own role (session invalidated).

"My profile" › "Relogin" opens the login window without closing the main window. Since the system allows only one active session at a time, if you try to log in while your session is still open the notice "A user is already logged in. Please log out before starting another session." is shown.
To log in with another user, first log out of the current session. The X of the Relogin window only closes that window, without leaving the application.

consejos: Always log out when leaving your workstation: everything done with your user is recorded under your name in the Audit Log.
If you changed the language during the session, it will be remembered for your next login.
